description: We're an ambitious team at the Kochi 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge, tackling the "Abandoned but not Forgotten" storytelling challenge! We blend technology and art to build out-of-the-box solutions. We're actively looking for passionate teammates to complete our roster. If you have skills in Coding, Software, Hardware, AI & ML, Game Dev, Animation, Design, Videography, or love space topics (Planets, Moons, Sun), join us to build something amazing!
summary: Abandoned but Not Forgotten is a scrolling story told in the first person by NASA’s Opportunity rover, left behind on Mars. It was designed for 90 sols and instead worked for 5,111. The story follows five short acts: landing in Eagle Crater, finding hematite “blueberries” that show Mars was once wet, driving 28.06 miles, going silent in the 2018 global dust storm, and the question of what we leave behind on other worlds. Real NASA numbers (distance, sols, dust opacity, final power) are woven into the story. Narration, animations and illustrations make it feel like a short film you scroll through. It works on phones, in classrooms and at outreach events.
details:
What it does
Abandoned, but Not Forgotten is a scrolling story told by NASA’s Opportunity rover, left behind on Mars. Opportunity was designed for 90 sols and worked for 5,111. Over five short acts, the rover narrates its landing in Eagle Crater, its discovery of hematite “blueberries” that show Mars was once wet, its 28.06-mile drive, the 2018 global dust storm that silenced it, and the question of what we leave behind on other worlds. Real mission numbers appear inside the story.

How it works
The story is one continuous web page. As the reader scrolls, each act brings its own effect: a starfield and Martian horizon on the title screen, an image that bounces in like a ball for the “hole in one” landing, a trail that draws itself behind the traverse map, a dust storm that builds in the dark act, and a quiet, breathing ending. Narration plays for each act, and a small rover drives across the screen as the page scrolls.

Benefits and intended impact
It turns an abandoned machine’s mission into something readers can feel, not just read about, which helps students and general audiences connect with space exploration history. It needs no sign-in or app and works on a phone, so it can be used in classrooms, libraries and outreach events.

Tools
HTML5, CSS3 and JavaScript (no framework), Canvas and SVG animation, scroll-triggered effects, MP3 narration, Netlify hosting and GitHub for the code.

How it is creative
The abandoned machine tells its own story, and the mood of the visuals follows the story, from busy and warm at landing to dark in the storm to quiet at the end. The reader controls the pace by scrolling.

Factors we considered

  • Accuracy: we checked key facts against NASA pages. For example, the rover’s distance is 28.06 miles, and the final power reading is given as “about 22 W” because sources differ slightly.
  • Accessibility and comfort: narration is optional, the site is mobile-first, and motion effects respect “reduce motion” settings.
  • Transparency: AI use is acknowledged (Claude for text and code, Narakeet and fish audio for the narration voice), and no AI-generated images are used.
  • Branding: the project uses no NASA logos or mission patches.
